chunks: And from him, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: In the case of a man who had four wives under him, and he divorced one, then married another before the divorced woman completed her waiting period (iddah), he said: 'He should keep her with her family until the divorced woman completes her term, and the other [new wife] begins a new waiting period. She is entitled to her dowry if he consummated the marriage with her; and if he did not consummate it with her, then her money is his, and there is no waiting period upon her. Then, if her family wishes, after the completion of her waiting period, they may marry her to him, and if they wish, they may not marry her to him.'

key_terms.الْعِدَّةَ: Waiting period (Iddah) for a divorced woman
key_terms.دَخَلَ بِهَا: He consummated the marriage with her

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when a man divorces one wife and marries another before the first wife's waiting period ends?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the divorce is not annulled but remains valid, allowing the husband to marry a new wife while the first completes her iddah in her family's home, a ruling that underscores the distinct legal status of each marriage in polygyny. The hadith highlights the autonomy of the first wife’s family to negotiate her remarriage to the same husband after the waiting period, reflecting the Shia emphasis on mutual consent and financial rights (mahr) tied to consummation. This narration is foundational in distinguishing between the effects of revocable divorce and the procedural requirements for maintaining multiple concurrent marriages.
